PullRequest.Title: agentHost: restore authentication on transport reconnect
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #339229. The transport can now reconnect, but the client still assumed that a remembered client ID meant authentication survived on the replacement connection. A host that requires authentication again can reject later requests with `AuthRequired`, while local authentication caching prevents a new authentication request from being sent.

- Restore required or previously established authentication for replay and snapshot reconnects, not only fresh initialization.
- Defer protected subscriptions reported missing before authentication, and restore subscriptions omitted from handshake snapshots after authentication.
- Keep recovery in progress and queued actions buffered until authentication and subscription restoration settle.
- Preserve errors for resources that remain missing or forbidden after authentication; keep the existing behavior for connections without authentication.
- Add six regressions covering cached/resolved credentials, replay/snapshot recovery, traffic ordering, response continuity through turn completion, and terminal subscription failures.

## Validation

- Four new regressions reproduced the old behavior before the fix: readiness was reported too early and protected subscriptions were marked unavailable.
- 321 related protocol-client, sandbox service, credential, and telemetry tests pass in Electron.
- 122 sandbox service/credential/telemetry tests pass in each of Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. The protocol-client suite is Electron-only and was excluded by the browser runner.
- Targeted TypeScript diagnostics, ESLint, whitespace checks, and pre-commit hygiene pass.
- Independent read-only review found no blocking issues.

## Manual verification pending

On mobile, open a sandbox chat, send a message, switch to another app, return, and send a follow-up. Verify recovery authenticates before messages are released and that responses remain visible after completion.

The supplied logs establish the post-reconnect authentication failure. They do not identify the chat-state update that removed an earlier streamed reply, so this PR does not claim that the separate disappearing-response symptom is conclusively resolved. Live mobile validation remains pending. The separately reported regular-tunnel recovery issue is also outside this fix.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Production wiring always configures the resolver for cloud sandboxes; the forced Mission Control refresh, 30-second limiter, and reconnect-gate ordering are explicit. Only the exact remote duration varies.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Mission Control network calls, authenticate RPCs, and provider authentication work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One forced cloud credential refresh and one authenticate RPC per cached authentication entry on every replacement transport; cost grows with reconnect frequency and credential count.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Higher resume latency and potentially about 30 seconds of blocked reconnect progress on closely spaced transport failures.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Ordinary replay reconnects reused host authentication and drained queued traffic; restoration ran only for fresh initialization or an interrupted restore pass.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every replacement transport with configured or cached authentication now awaits authentication restoration before outbox drain and Connected state, regardless of whether reconnect reported any authentication loss.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 955 newly makes restoration true from the mere presence of a resolver or cached credential, so even Replay with missing=[] enters the blocking authentication path.
Findings.Title: Avoid reminting credentials on every replay reconnect
Findings.Impact: An ordinary mobile resume or network flap now blocks queued cloud-sandbox chat traffic on a Mission Control request and host authentication even for Replay with missing=[]. A second flap within 30 seconds hits the refresh limiter, delaying recovery until a later retry.
Findings.Evidence: CloudSandboxConnectionFactory always supplies resolveInitialAuthentication. Its prepareAuthentication calls refreshAuthenticationCredentials when the current sealed token was previously used, which forces ICloudSandboxApiService.reconnect. CloudSandboxCredentialRefresher rejects another forced refresh within MIN_CREDENTIAL_REFRESH_DELAY_MS=30,000. This predicate ignores result.missing and AuthRequired, and reconnect awaits it before draining queued messages.
Findings.Recommendation: Restore only on a concrete loss signal, such as missing protected subscriptions or AuthRequired, while retaining fresh-initialize and interrupted-pass restoration; let Replay with no authentication debt drain immediately.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cloud-sandbox transport reconnect that returns Replay with no missing subscriptions, such as mobile app resume or a transient network change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Transport preparation/connect and the reconnect RPC must finish; the diff then synchronously gates outbox drain and Connected state on credential preparation/resolution and all authenticate RPCs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh Web PubSub and sealed GitHub credentials through ICloudSandboxApiService.reconnect.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Newly one forced Mission Control request per successful ordinary replacement transport when the previously used sealed token is still current; shared only with an already in-flight refresh and rejected inside the 30-second forced-refresh window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Ordinary Replay reconnects with no pending authentication restore did not invoke prepareAuthentication or the Mission Control refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks protocol authentication, reconnect completion, and all queued chat traffic.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send authenticate RPCs that fan out to matching host providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC per non-expired cached authentication key, issued in parallel after the single credential-preparation phase.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These RPCs ran after fresh initialization or interrupted restoration, not every ordinary Replay reconnect.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All RPCs settle before reconnect can drain its outbox or report Connected.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reconnect the logical protocol client over the replacement Web PubSub transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same reconnect RPC and transport setup occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required handshake work that precedes the new authentication work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Transport-failure frequency and the number of cached protected-resource credentials; even one credential triggers the production cloud refresh path.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Credential refresh is serialized before authentication; authentication keys are then sent concurrently with Promise.all. Reconnect attempts themselves are sequenced by the reconnect state/backoff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm transport credentials normally let prepareReconnect avoid I/O, but the newly unconditional authentication pass defeats that warm path by requiring a fresh sealed token. Forced refreshes are coalesced only while in flight and are rejected for 30 seconds after the last refresh.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added predicate, production callback wiring, API boundary, limiter, and reconnect gate were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Mission Control and provider-authentication duration varies by network and provider count, but the extra request is certain; a second flap within the explicit 30-second limiter has a deterministic failed-attempt mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable high-severity latency regression because authentication is repeated without any loss signal, including Replay responses with missing=[], and blocks the resume critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reconnect where protected session/chat subscriptions are reported missing before authentication
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Reconnect handshake completes, authentication is restored, then every active omitted/missing subscription is re-subscribed and snapshotted before queued actions are released.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh cloud credentials when necessary and authenticate protected resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cloud credential refresh in the production cloud path and one authenticate RPC per cached key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: On ordinary reconnect, missing subscriptions were immediately marked unavailable without reauthentication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before protected subscription restoration can start.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Issue subscribe RPCs and receive full snapshots for active channels omitted by the handshake.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC per effective active missing/omitted resource after URI deduplication. Session subscriptions run concurrently as one phase; chat and other resources run concurrently in the next phase.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Replay-missing resources were marked unavailable; fresh-initialize restoration already used this per-resource path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The complete session phase and then chat/other phase are awaited before reconnect completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Deserialize and apply one returned state snapshot per restored resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One snapshot per active missing resource, with payload size determined by session, chat, terminal, or changeset state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No snapshots were fetched for ordinary Replay-missing resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Snapshot application is part of each awaited subscribe completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective active subscription count, not holder refcount: normally session plus chat for each open/hydrating chat, with observed terminal and changeset resources adding distinct channels.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All session restores run in parallel first; chat and non-chat restores then run in parallel together. There is no shared limiter, but active-resource cardinality is UI-lifecycle bounded and the work is necessary to restore previously unavailable state.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The active-subscription map deduplicates holders by resource. Successful snapshots delete restore debt; disconnected attempts retain debt for retry; terminal NotFound/PermissionDenied removes debt and marks the subscription missing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for boundary count and ordering from the implementation; moderate for upper-end real-world active-resource counts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large chats and many observed terminal resources can increase bytes and fan-out, but no evidence establishes a separate unacceptable regression beyond the unconditional authentication finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: this fan-out is newly exercised for protected missing resources but directly implements required state restoration, is deduplicated by active resource, and lacks evidence of an independent performance failure.

Scenarios.Scenario: Fresh initial connection or reconnect after the host forgot the client
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Transport connect, initialize, optional authentication, then queued messages are released; fresh reconnect may additionally restore omitted active subscriptions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize the protocol client and obtain root/initial snapshots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initialize RPC for initial connection, or one fallback initialize after a reconnect NotFound.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same initialization boundary existed before the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Prepare credentials and authenticate cached/resolved resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One preparation plus one RPC per non-expired authentication key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Fresh initialization already restored authentication and awaited it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks readiness as before for fresh initialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe channels omitted from a fresh handshake snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per deduplicated active omitted resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Fresh host-restart recovery already marked omitted channels and restored them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks fresh reconnect completion until snapshots settle.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cached authentication-key count and deduplicated active subscriptions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Authentication keys are parallel; subscription restoration uses the existing session-first two-phase parallel grouping.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Authentication entries remain cached until expiry or explicit token removal; active subscriptions are refcounted and deduplicated. Fresh snapshots settle outstanding restore debt.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider and snapshot costs vary, but this scenario's boundary placement and cardinality are materially unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression in this scenario; the method rename/generalization preserves the pre-diff fresh-initialization cost.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and traced reconnect, cloud credential refresh, authentication provider fan-out, active-subscription lifecycle, snapshot restoration, cache state, concurrency, and all network/serialization boundaries. Submitted one high-confidence reconnect-latency finding; no performance-fix learning record applies.
